name: tag
summary: Compact label for categorization or removable selections. Used as a plain tag; color variants are broken.

variants.name: numeric
variants.what: count/metric tag in the numeric font (tabular figures)

variant.note: ColorPalette keys; colored variants illegible (F2) — use colorClasses instead

numeric.note: count/metric tag — renders JetBrains Mono (--numeric-font-family) with tabular figures (the product .numeric-value). Pair with rounded for a count pill.

colorClasses.note: The working colored-tag mechanism — colored text on a tint, themes both modes. Apply via class, not variant.

styling.plainBg: --tag-bg-color (#e3e8f2 light / #2b394f dark, themed) — the neutral tag-primary bg. NOTE: --tag-bg is a DIFFERENT token (#ecf1f9) used by the broken `variant` prop (F2).

do: Use a plain tag for labels; :closable=true for removable chips; :rounded for pills.
dont: Assuming info/neutral exist (F1); forgetting closable defaults to true (F5).
decisionFlow: User types/adds tags? -> LooseTags (input), not Tag.
Colored category label? -> MTag + tag-* class.
A COUNT / metric value (not a text label)? -> add `numeric` (JetBrains Mono, tabular figures).

closable.useWhen: a selection the user can dismiss (filters, picked items)
closable.note: closable defaults true; display tags need :closable=false

colored(tag-*).dontUse: the color variant PROP (broken/illegible F2) — use the class

tag-red.useWhen: Color-coding a negative/critical category label with a red tint — the most common colored tag (75×). Applied as a class (MTag class="tag-red"), legible in both themes.
tag-red.dontUse: Don't use the color `variant` prop (variant="error" is broken/illegible — F2). If the chip is driven by a status STRING (error/down/failed/critical/stopped/offline), use MStatusTag instead — its TAG_MAP resolves those to tag-red automatically.
tag-red.example: A red-tinted 'Failed' job-run label or a 'Critical'/'Down' state chip in an inventory or alert grid.

tag-green.useWhen: Color-coding a positive/success category with a green tint (57×). Apply as MTag class="tag-green".
tag-green.dontUse: Don't use variant="success" (broken — F2). For a status STRING (up/success/active/enabled/completed/online), let MStatusTag map it to tag-green instead of hand-applying the class.
tag-green.example: A green 'Up'/'Enabled'/'Succeeded' chip in a monitor or job status grid.

tag-yellow.useWhen: Color-coding a warning or transitional state with a yellow tint (15×). Apply as MTag class="tag-yellow".
tag-yellow.dontUse: Don't use variant="warning" (broken — F2). Note MStatusTag's TAG_MAP maps halted/paused/queued/aborted/starting to tag-yellow, but it lacks true severity 'warning' — for severity LEVELS use the Severity component, not this class.

tag-orange.useWhen: Color-coding a caution/intermediate state with an orange tint (9×). Apply as MTag class="tag-orange".
tag-orange.dontUse: Don't use variant="orange" (broken — F2). Prefer tag-yellow for transient/queued states and tag-red for hard failures; orange is for the in-between (suspended/fair).
tag-orange.example: An orange 'Suspended' monitor state or a 'Fair' quality-rating chip.

tag-purple.useWhen: A rarely-used purple tint reserved for the 'unreachable' condition (1× — maps from --severity-unreachable). Apply as MTag class="tag-purple".
tag-purple.dontUse: Don't reach for purple as a generic color — it carries the 'unreachable' meaning. Use tag-red/tag-green/tag-yellow for ordinary category coding, and the Severity component for severity levels.
tag-purple.example: A purple 'Unreachable' chip for a monitor that cannot be contacted (statusMap: unreachable → tag-purple).

tag-unknown.useWhen: A neutral 'unknown' tint (2×) for indeterminate state — text is --severity-unknown on a light tint. Apply as MTag class="tag-unknown".
tag-unknown.dontUse: Don't use for a plain neutral metadata label — that's tag-primary. Reserve tag-unknown for genuinely unknown/indeterminate status.
tag-unknown.example: An 'Unknown' status chip where a monitor's state can't be determined (statusMap: unknown → tag-unknown).

tag-primary.useWhen: A neutral chip (NOT blue) — the default gray tag on --tag-bg-color, for read-only category/metadata labels and neutral states (49×). Apply as MTag class="tag-primary" (or forcePrimary on MStatusTag).
tag-primary.dontUse: Don't use it for a semantic status — pick tag-red/green/yellow (or MStatusTag) so the color carries meaning. Don't confuse it with a blue/brand chip; it renders neutral gray.
tag-primary.example: A neutral device-category or environment metadata chip, or a 'Maintenance'/'Connected'/'Standby' state (statusMap maps those to tag-primary).

MStatusTag.useWhen: The chip is driven by a status STRING (up/down/critical/paused/success/failed…) — MStatusTag looks the value up in TAG_MAP and renders the right tag-* color + capitalized label automatically. Always rounded and non-closable.
MStatusTag.dontUse: For true severity LEVELS (critical/major/warning/clear) use the Severity component — TAG_MAP lacks major/warning/clear and silently falls through to a plain gray tag (F7). For a static hand-picked color label, apply a tag-* class directly rather than routing through a status string. Beware F7: poweredoff→'Up', poweredon→'Down' (intentional inversion), and unmapped statuses render a silent plain tag.
MStatusTag.example: A monitor's Up/Down state in the monitor status sidebar and instance grids: <MStatusTag :status="row.status" />.

used-count-pill.useWhen: A rounded neutral COUNT chip — primary-text on a tint, always :rounded (48×) — for showing how many times something is used/referenced.
used-count-pill.dontUse: Don't use it to convey status or severity (use MStatusTag or a tag-* color class). It's a neutral count pill, not a semantic color, and it's distinct from the tag-* color classes.
used-count-pill.example: A '3 used' count pill next to a template/credential in a usage list.

numeric.useWhen: a COUNT or metric tag (log-type counts, used-counts, percentages) — the numeric font aligns figures
numeric.dontUse: a text label tag (leave numeric off; text uses the normal font)
numeric.example: the Log tree counts (6.77 M, 653.32 K) render in JetBrains Mono; default 4px squarish, add rounded for a pill

knownIssues: F2 (high): colored variants are illegible — bg forced to --tag-bg regardless of variant, variant only sets white text → white on #e3e8f2 in light. Use MStatusTag for status.
F4 (high, a11y): remove × is an <a> with no href/role/aria-label/tabindex — not focusable, unlabeled. Make it a real button + aria-label + focus ring (SF-001).
F1 (medium): variants = ColorPalette keys only (no info/neutral); static hex differs from severity tokens.
F5 (medium): closable defaults to true — display tags get an unexpected ×.
F3 (low): Tag.vue applies misspelled class 'neutral-ligher' so the .neutral-lighter themed override never matches.
F7 (low): MStatusTag textMap inverts poweredoff->'Up'/poweredon->'Down'; status not in TAG_MAP renders a silent plain tag (no colour). Add an unknown/default mapping.

SF-002 (medium, tooling, FIXED 2026-06-07): Storybook now runs the app's PostCSS (tailwindcss+autoprefixer) via postcss-loader, so Tailwind utilities (incl. MStatusTag inline-flex alignment) render like the product. See findings/SF-002.

members.MStatusTag: VARIANT of Tag (not a separate component, D12). _base-status-tag.vue, 30x/28 files. Maps status string -> tag-* colour + Capitalize(label). Props: status (String|Number), forcePrimary (Boolean). Always rounded+non-closable. LIVE in Storybook (Atoms/Tag/Examples -> 'Status / severity'). Quirks F7: poweredoff->'Up'/poweredon->'Down'; unmapped status -> silent plain tag.
members.SelectedItemPills: dropdown-trigger/ — teal ant-tag-has-color picker pills, truncated, +N overflow popover (maxItems default 1); teal via --main-tags-* in input.less (:tags adds .loose-tags-input). LIVE in Storybook (Atoms/Tag/Examples → 'Selected pills'); full behaviour with DropdownPicker

changelog.change: Added `numeric` — a count/metric tag in the numeric font (--numeric-font-family JetBrains Mono + tnum), matching the product .numeric-value used on count tags (e.g. the Log tree). Reused by obs-side-menu tree counts.

changelog: 2026-06-06: full deep-dive — real variant set found, colored variants measured illegible (F2); examples refocused on plain/removable; findings F1-F5 + SF-001; Option B pages.
2026-06-07: family surfaced in Storybook — ColoredTags (tag-* classes) + SelectedItemPills teal +N picker pills (verified teal #cdf1ed/#218b81 + +N overflow).

statusMap.$usage: MStatusTag: <MStatusTag :status="row.status" /> -> looks up status.toLowerCase() in `map` for the tag-* colour class; label = Capitalize(status) unless overridden by `textOverrides`. Unmapped status -> plain tag (silent). `forcePrimary` forces tag-primary.
statusMap.quirk: F7 — poweredoff renders label 'Up' (green), poweredon renders 'Down' (red). Intentional inversion.

tagColors.$note: Each tag-* class = a TEXT token (resolve via tokens/variables.json) + a bg. Most bgs are a 20% rgba tint of the text hue (literal); tag-primary/unknown/purple use bg tokens.

statusMap.severityNote: For severity LEVELS (critical/major/warning/clear/up/down/…) use the **Severity** component (severity.json) — NOT MStatusTag. MStatusTag's TAG_MAP lacks major/warning/clear (they fall through to a grey plain tag, F7).

a11y.summary: Plain tag = non-interactive <span> (fine as a label); default contrast legible in both themes.
issues: Removable tag × is not keyboard-accessible (keyboard/AT blocker).
a11y.$note: Catalogue-wide gap SF-001 = no visible :focus-visible ring; tracked in findings/.
